name: mushroomed lentils french
instructions:
One of two recipes built on the MUSHROOMED LENTIL BASE — the shared gravy core of PUREED MUSHROOMS + WHOLE LENTILS + TOMATO PASTE + DARK BOUILLON + BUTTER + FLOUR. The base is a vegetarian way of making something 'meaty' in a stew or pie, but it's NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN — each version injects flavor from its register. THIS is the FRENCH version: MUSTARD + CREAM + POTATO do the injection. See [[mushroomed-lentils-german]] for the dark-ale sibling.

=== THE MUSHROOMED LENTIL BASE (SHARED CORE) ===

- pureed portabella mushrooms (food processor or blender)
- whole lentils
- tomato paste (small, cooked hard — necessary but should NOT be tasted)
- dark bouillon / stock
- butter
- flour (light roux)

=== FRENCH INJECTION ===

- dijon mustard + heavy cream (stirred in near the end — SILENT; the lentil/potato starch absorbs them)
- potatoes (finely chopped — the sweetness and savoriness the base lacks)

=== VEGETABLES (ASSORT AUTOMATICALLY BY REGISTER) ===

- The french version likes the traditional ONION / CELERY / CARROT soffrito.
- LEEKS are welcome too — they bridge both registers.

=== HERBS ===

- FRESH THYME preferred. Rosemary also allowed. Nothing else — fine herbs are clashing (see notes).

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SOFFRITO IN BUTTER + OLIVE OIL: sauté finely chopped yellow onion, celery, and carrots (and leek if using) until softened.
2. PUREED MUSHROOMS: puree the portabellas, add to the pot, and cook down until reduced and deepened in color.
3. TOMATO PASTE — SMALL, COOKED HARD: a small spoonful, cooked into the fat until it darkens a shade. It should not be tasteable in the finished stew.
4. FLOUR — LIGHT ROUX: dust flour over the base and stir to coat.
5. HERBS: fresh thyme (or a light hand of rosemary). Salt and black pepper.
6. POTATOES + LENTILS: fold in finely diced potatoes and lentils together (same cook rate).
7. DARK BOUILLON / STOCK: pour in generously — the primary liquid.
8. SLOW COOK covered until lentils and potatoes are tender.
9. MUSTARD + CREAM — NEAR THE END: a spoonful of dijon and a splash of cream, stirred in. Both silent in the finished stew.
10. OPTIONAL STARCH SLURRY at the end if the broth reads thin (usually not needed — the roux + potatoes carry it).
notes:
=== WHY 'MUSHROOMED LENTILS' LEADS THE NAME ===

The MUSHROOMED LENTIL BASE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour) is the identity — it's what separates this pair of recipes from the cookbook's other lentil dishes (e.g. a classic french le puy lentil preparation, which has no gravy core at all). The base is the vegetarian meaty-gravy mechanism; the register (french here, anglo-germanic in the sibling) is the flavor injected on top.

THE BASE IS NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN — this was proven by experiment (stock + vegetables + gravy base alone makes a dull stew). Each version needs its injection kit:
- FRENCH (this recipe): mustard + cream + potato.
- ANGLO-GERMANIC ([[mushroomed-lentils-german]]): dark ale + pickle juice + cumin/caraway seeds.

=== THE FRENCH INJECTION — MUSTARD + CREAM + POTATO ===

- POTATOES: add a sweetness and savoriness the base doesn't have. Finely diced (small dice) so they cook with the lentils and dissolve starch into the broth. Not filler — the missing flavor dimension.
- MUSTARD + CREAM: do a ton of heavy lifting, SILENTLY — done carefully you don't taste either, because the starch load from lentils + potatoes absorbs them (same silent-ingredient logic as [[spinach-ricotta]]'s miso/nooch rule). They round and enrich without announcing themselves.

=== TOMATO — NECESSARY BUT SHOULDN'T BE TASTED ===

Tomato paste is part of the shared core: its darkened concentration does real depth-and-color work. But it should NOT read as tomato in the finished stew. Two mechanisms keep it in line:
- SMALL QUANTITY, cooked hard into the fat.
- THE PUREED MUSHROOMS TAME IT: the mushroom base grounds and darkens so tomato contributes depth without running the show. (Same mechanism in the anglo-germanic sibling, where dark ale helps too.)
Counterintuitively, this french version needs LESS tomato paste than the anglo one, even though the anglo one looks darker — french ingredients mesh with tomato; the anglo version's bitter base fights it and needs more. Calibrate by register, not color.

=== VEGETABLES — ONION / CELERY / CARROT (LEEKS BRIDGE) ===

The french version takes the traditional soffrito: onion + celery + carrot. Leeks are welcome in both versions of this pair — they bridge the two registers.

=== WINE — A RATATOUILLE SITUATION: WORKS BUT UNNECESSARY ===

White wine went through the full arc here (primary → clashing → re-diagnosed as balance-dependent). Final stance: it's a RATATOUILLE SITUATION — wine works, but the dish doesn't need it, and the version without is just as good. Save the wine for dishes where it does structural work. (If you do add it: modest amount, and make sure the butter/flour/potato balance is present to absorb it.)

=== HERBS — FRESH THYME PREFERRED; ROSEMARY ALLOWED; FINE HERBS CLASHING ===

The herb slot for both recipes in this pair is ROSEMARY/THYME ONLY. The french version PREFERS FRESH THYME; rosemary is allowed (light hand). FINE HERBS ARE CLASHING — parsley, basil, tarragon, dill all read wrong against the mushroomed gravy base. (The anglo-germanic sibling prefers rosemary instead.)

=== REFERENCE — VALIDATED EXPERIMENTS (READ-ONLY LOG) ===

The experiments that produced this recipe remain valid; kept condensed for reference:
- STOCK + VEGETABLES + GRAVY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — the injection kit is required (this is what forced the mustard/cream/potato discovery).
- BUTTER + FLOUR + MUSTARD was the original 'generic to home run' enrichment finding; cream joined later.
- MUSTARD-AND-MUSHROOM PAIRING: dijon + mushroom fills the same structural role miso + mushroom fills in [[mushroomed-lentils-british]] — fermented condiment + mushroom = enhanced meat-analog umami. When a mushroom-forward dish reads flat, reach for the register-appropriate fermented condiment.
- WINE RE-DIAGNOSIS: earlier wine failures were balance failures (too much wine or not enough starch/butter), not the wine itself.
- PUREED-NOT-CHOPPED: chopped mushrooms give a chunkier, less integrated dish; the puree is the base's mechanism.
- STOCK PREFERRED, BOUILLON OKAY: real stock has the gentler layered body; bouillon works with a lighter hand than the package says.
- The broader three-register theory lives in articles/stew-registers.md (read-only reference).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[mushroomed-lentils-german]]: the same base with the anglo-germanic injection (dark ale + pickle juice + cumin/caraway). The contrast pair.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of the anglo-germanic register.
- [[mushroomed-lentils-british]]: same lentil + mushroom umami DNA in a baked-log pastry format.
- [[french-chicken-soup]]: the committed-french-broth cousin with chicken.
- italian-minestrone-soup: the committed-italian-tomato path — what this recipe's demoted-tomato logic deliberately is not.
